scope: Strict identity and reconstruction-suitability audit of the 12 batch-1 reference photographs.

method.identity: The selected source caption/metadata was checked against at least two separately published results. Characteristic front details, production period and model-family relationship were compared; a search-result label alone was not accepted as proof.
method.suitability: A pass requires the radiator/grille, both headlamp positions, bumper or front cross-member, bonnet/nose contour and enough bilateral geometry for a symmetric frontal reconstruction to be visible.
method.verdicts: pass means the photograph is suitable for the catalog ID. reject means the model/generation is wrong or the front cannot support reconstruction. confidence records residual uncertainty without changing the verdict.

items.reason: The Commons file identifies a 1925 Laurin & Klement–Škoda 110 Phaeton. Škoda's 2025 Classic Days material independently confirms the 110 debuted in 1925, used several body styles including phaeton/roadster-type open bodies, and that the museum car is an early first-series example. The photographed dual-brand-era radiator and period chassis/body architecture agree with those records.
items.frontSuitability: Good three-quarter front. The complete radiator, both separate headlamps, front axle/cross-member, both front fenders and bonnet sides are visible. Perspective correction is required, but bilateral geometry is recoverable.

verificationSources.finding: Official Škoda history confirms model, 1925–1929 period, body variety and dual Laurin & Klement/Škoda branding after the merger.
Separately published official press kit describes the preserved first-series museum 110 and its period construction.
Independent museum record identifies a separately photographed 1925 L&K 110 phaeton and corroborates the body, chassis and production period.

items.reason: The selected file is explicitly a Škoda 110 R front. Both Škoda's official history and Automobil Revue independently document four front lamps from model year 1973; the selected car has exactly the late-series four-lamp face, central narrow badge strip and period bumper.
items.frontSuitability: Excellent direct front. Both main lamps, inner auxiliary lamps, central trim, bumper, bonnet and windshield base are visible with minimal perspective distortion.

verificationSources.finding: Official Škoda account confirms the 1970–1980 110 R and the four-lamp front introduced in January 1973.
Independent specialist magazine distinguishes the earlier two-lamp face from the four-lamp 1973-on front shown in the selected photo.

items.reason: The Commons file identifies a Škoda Tudor and the visible dense split grille is specifically consistent with a 1101. Škoda's official 1101/1102 histories confirm the family and note that the 1102 used modified bumpers and a plainer grille, supporting the selected image as a valid 1101 representative of the grouped catalog entry.
items.frontSuitability: Good close three-quarter front. Both lamps, the full split grille, bonnet center, bumper and both fender contours are visible; the view is oblique and cropped behind the front axle, but contains all front-design evidence needed.

verificationSources.finding: Official history confirms the 1946–1952 1101/1102 family and describes the 1102's plainer grille and modified bumpers.
A later official museum feature independently repeats the 1101/1102 visual distinction and identifies the preserved 1101 form.
Independent museum record and photographs corroborate the 1101 Tudor identity, rounded body and 1946–1952 period.

items.reason: The Commons event file and visible display card identify the vehicle as a Škoda 1200. Official Škoda material and Auto.cz independently confirm the 1200 body and its evolution into the nearly identical 1201. The selected car has the early smooth nose and inset horizontal trim of the documented 1200/early Sedan form. Confidence is medium because many surviving 1200s acquired later indicators or trim during service, and the photograph alone cannot prove every fitted detail is factory-original.
items.frontSuitability: Good three-quarter front. Nose profile, both headlamps, both bumper halves, central trim and bonnet are visible. The angle is oblique but adequate for frontal reconstruction.

verificationSources.finding: Official history confirms the 1952 Škoda 1200 and the later 1201 modernization within the same closely related body family.
Independent model history lists the gradual visual changes from 1200 to 1201, explaining why restored examples can combine details.

items.reason: Although the legacy Commons filename says 1200, the file description/structured identification says 1201. The photographed protruding door handles, front indicators and grille/type-badge treatment agree with independently documented 1201 changes. Confidence remains medium because 1200/1201 bodies are extremely close and restorations often mix trim; the photo metadata and visible features together, rather than the filename, support 1201.
items.frontSuitability: Good three-quarter front. Both lamps, indicators, grille strips/type badge, bumper guards, bonnet and both fender forms are clear. Yellow auxiliary lamps are removable accessories and do not obscure the factory face.

verificationSources.finding: Independent specialist history identifies 1201 changes including external door handles, central mask designation and newer wheels.
Independent history separately documents protruding handles, indicators beside lamps and thinner lamp rims on the 1201.
Official Škoda history confirms the updated 1201 production model and its relationship to the 1200.

items.reason: The Commons file and the windshield display identify Škoda 1202. Independent sources confirm the 1202's new wide grille and 1961–1973 production, and a specialist source describes the exact early grille layout visible here: seven horizontal bars, four vertical elements and bumper guards on early cars.
items.frontSuitability: Excellent near-direct front. Both lamps and indicators, complete wide grille, split bumper, bonnet and windshield outline are unobstructed. The windshield papers do not cover the front design.

verificationSources.finding: Dedicated 1202 history describes the early seven-horizontal/four-vertical grille and bumper guards visible in the reference.
Independent history confirms the 1202 body, wide new front grille and successor relationship to 1200/1201.

Official Škoda histories confirm the model's 1968 launch and cab-over one-box construction; an independent Auto.cz history confirms rectangular lamps came only in the mid-1980s, so the round-lamp reference is correct for the catalog's original Škoda-era generation.
items.frontSuitability: Excellent exact front with both headlamps, grille, indicators, bumper, mirror arms and cab outline visible. Yellow auxiliary lamps are period accessories but do not obscure key geometry and can be omitted.

verificationSources.finding: Official Škoda account confirms the 1968 production model, one-box cab-over body and period.

items.reason: The selected image is an official Škoda 130 L factory front. It is a valid representative for the grouped catalog model.

items.reason: Auta5P identifies the selected head-on car as a Škoda 445. Independent histories confirm that 445 was visually the same closed-body family as 440, while 450 was the related open model, and document the characteristic paired kidney grille of the pre-1959 range. A 445 is therefore a correct production member and suitable representative for this grouped catalog entry.
items.frontSuitability: Excellent direct front. Both main lamps, paired upper grille openings, complete lower grille and bumper, bonnet, indicators and full body width are visible. Yellow auxiliary lamps are accessories and can be omitted without losing factory geometry.

verificationSources.finding: Dedicated model history identifies the 440/445 front by its paired kidney openings and confirms shared appearance within the Spartak family.
